title: Architecture Patterns
description: Learn common AWS architecture patterns including 3-tier, serverless, microservices, and event-driven designs.

data.text: Architecture patterns are proven solutions to common design problems. AWS offers services that support many well-known patterns, and choosing the right pattern helps you build scalable, reliable systems.
A classic pattern with three layers: presentation (frontend), application (backend logic), and data (database). Each tier scales independently, making it a solid starting point for many applications.

data.caption: Classic 3-tier architecture with web, application, and database layers
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Users] --> B[Presentation Tier: CloudFront + ALB]
    B --> C[Application Tier: EC2 / ECS / Lambda]
    C --> D[Data Tier: RDS / DynamoDB]
    C --> E[Cache: ElastiCache]
    F[CDN: S3 + CloudFront] --> A

data.text: Serverless removes the need to manage servers entirely. You write functions (Lambda) and connect them through events. AWS handles provisioning, scaling, and patching.

data.caption: Serverless architecture with API Gateway, Lambda, and managed services
data.definition:
flowchart TB
    A[Users] --> B[API Gateway]
    B -->|HTTP Request| C[Lambda Function]
    C -->|Read/Write| D[DynamoDB]
    C -->|Async| E[SQS Queue]
    E --> F[Lambda Processor]
    F -->|Store| G[S3]
    H[Event: S3 Upload] --> I[Lambda Trigger]
    I -->|Process| C

data.title: Patterns Overview
items: **Microservices** — break the app into small, independent services communicating via APIs
**Event-Driven** — services react to events (e.g., S3 upload, DynamoDB stream)
**Event Sourcing** — store all changes as events; reconstruct state by replaying
**CQRS** — separate read and write models for optimized performance
**Queue-Based** — decouple producers and consumers with SQS or SNS
**Pub/Sub** — broadcast events to multiple subscribers with SNS
**Fanout** — SNS topic triggers multiple Lambda functions

terms.definition: Small, independent services that communicate over a network.
An architecture where services react to events rather than direct calls.
Command Query Responsibility Segregation — separates read and write operations.
A pattern where one event triggers multiple downstream processes.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: 3-tier is a solid starting point for traditional applications
Microservices enable independent scaling and deployment
Event-driven patterns decouple services and improve resilience
